tagline: A creekside county seat and a lighthouse isolated by the bay
intro: Route 14 runs through Mathews as Main Street before continuing toward New Point Comfort at the mouth of the York River. This is a peninsula landscape: Mathews County is almost entirely surrounded by water, with Mobjack Bay along its southern side. Inland, the county has few hills outside its northern section near the Gloucester boundary.

The county seat began as Westville, established around 1700 beside tidal Put-in Creek. When Mathews County was created in 1791, Westville became its seat, later taking the Mathews name. Off the peninsula’s tip, New Point Comfort Light was finished in 1804. Erosion and a 1933 hurricane eventually left its tower isolated on a small parcel of land.

From Mathews, follow Route 14 south toward Bavon. There, Point Road branches toward New Point Comfort Natural Area Preserve, while Route 14 turns toward Bayside and ends at Bayside Wharf on Davis Creek.

moments.title: Mathews
moments.text: Mathews began as Westville, a settlement established around 1700 on tidal Put-in Creek. The creek feeds the East River and, through it, Mobjack Bay. Westville became the new county’s seat in 1791. The brick courthouse followed in 1792–1795, a T-shaped building in the Federal style. Its square also includes an 1859 clerk’s office and a former jail later used as the sheriff’s office. The town is still known both as Mathews Court House and simply Mathews. The square’s later buildings also include the county library, which dates to the year 1930.

moments.title: Bethel Beach
moments.text: Bethel Beach brings beach, low dune and salt marsh together in a 105-acre natural area preserve beside the Chesapeake Bay. These habitats support rare marsh birds and colonial nesting birds. They also shelter two globally rare species: the northeastern beach tiger beetle and sea-beach knotweed. The Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation owns and maintains the preserve.
moments.notice: Beach, low dunes and salt marsh form neighboring habitats.

moments.title: New Point Comfort Light
moments.text: New Point Comfort Light stands surrounded by water, visible from a walkway at the southern tip of Mathews County. Its builder, Elzy Burroughs, bought the entire island after a dispute over the lighthouse site, then sold the government the acres it needed. The New Point Comfort tower was finished in 1804. Erosion made a boat necessary to reach it by 1839, and the 1933 hurricane cut through the island. The light was deactivated in 1963 and transferred to the county in 1975. After a lengthy restoration, it was relit in October 2021.
moments.notice: The lighthouse tower stands offshore, separated from the peninsula by water.
